policy: Standards are normative requirements for future implementation; only items tagged implemented-in-prototype have code enforcement.

rules: Use bg, en, de as supported language identifiers; accept valid BCP-47 variants and normalize to supported base language.
Never infer locale from IP address.
Strict JSON parsing on API and journal boundaries; bounded payload size and no credentials.
Use UTC ISO8601 timestamp with Z and millisecond precision in journal.
Reject invalid or stale timestamps in HA status.
Normalize identifiers/locale keys using NFC for indexing while preserving original user-visible text.
Do not normalize signed bytes or audit evidence.
Use locale-specific rules for plurals and number/date formatting rather than assembling strings.
Maintain placeholder parity across BG, EN, DE.
Use parameterized messages with exact placeholder contracts; migrate gradually rather than change existing dictionary semantics.
Support safe escaping and test all locale substitutions.
Version schemas and validate all structured incident/recovery events before ingestion.
Document new guardian read-only and future apply endpoints with role requirements and error responses.
Use stable type, source, id, time, subject and data fields; avoid PII and secrets.
Use stable semantic conventions and low-cardinality labels with opt-in exporters.
Offline collection must work without any exporter.
Accessible names and labels, keyboard access, focus management, high-contrast and clear destructive-action confirmation.
Explicit authorization, CSRF protection, immutable decision evidence and least privilege; no silent crossing of trust boundaries.
Bind candidate fixes to exact source commit, build provenance and reproducible test artifacts.
Honor existing hAPI version source and release gates; do not silently change the version format.
